books.section: President Obama and Health Care Reform
Threat of Terrorism, Increase of Presidential Power, and Economic Crisis (2001-2016)

options.text: To give the federal government control of all hospitals
options.misconception: The act did not take over hospitals.

options.text: To end all private health insurance in the United States
options.misconception: Private insurers kept selling plans on the exchanges.

options.text: To raise taxes on every American worker
options.misconception: The act was a health care law, not a general tax increase.

options.text: To reduce the number of Americans without health insurance

rationales.A: The act regulated insurance and expanded coverage. It did not take over hospitals.
rationales.B: Private insurers kept selling plans through the exchanges. The act did not end private insurance.
rationales.C: The act dealt with health insurance. It was not a general tax increase on every worker.
rationales.D: The account says the exchanges and the Medicaid expansion brought insurance to over 31 million Americans. That result is the purpose the law was written to reach.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what problem the law addressed. The account says it set up exchanges and expanded Medicaid.
2. Background: before the law, tens of millions of Americans had no health insurance.
3. The result given is that over 31 million Americans gained insurance, and the uninsured rate fell from 18 percent to 10 percent.
4. Taking over hospitals, ending private insurance, and taxing every worker all go beyond what the account describes.
Remember: a law that adds ways to get insurance aims at the uninsured.

stem: Why did the Affordable Care Act expand Medicaid and set up insurance exchanges?

stimulus.source_note: Photograph: official White House photograph, March 23, 2010. Public domain (U.S. federal government work). Account paraphrased from the grounding books (Barron's Premium 2027 Ch. 11; 5 Steps 2024 Ch. 30).
stimulus.text:
Photograph of President Barack Obama signing the Affordable Care Act on March 23, 2010, seated at a desk in the East Room of the White House, with Vice President Joe Biden and Speaker Nancy Pelosi among those standing behind him.

Paraphrase of a secondary account: The Affordable Care Act, passed in March 2010, set up health insurance exchanges and expanded Medicaid to cover more low-income Americans. The Supreme Court upheld its major parts. According to the Department of Health and Human Services, over 31 million Americans gained health insurance through the act, and the uninsured rate for non-elderly Americans fell from 18 percent in 2010 to 10 percent in 2016.

The act stayed controversial: Republicans opposed it and tried to repeal it, and premiums rose for some people who did not receive subsidies. In the same years, Congress passed the Dodd-Frank Act of 2010 to regulate financial markets and protect consumers after the Great Recession.
